summary: Tested DiscKit full-text search (build, plan, reader API and UI), the frozen PyInstaller app, the packaging files, the backend kit endpoints and the /burn KitSection. 24 of 25 pytest checks pass (new file test_disckit_fulltext.py). Build with full text gives fulltext:true, fulltext_docs=611, and docs+fts tables. --no-fulltext gives fulltext:false and the API returns available:false. Bowline is ranked first. Multi-word search, prefix on the last word (trefo -> Trefoil knot), paging with no overlap, empty q, and 12 special-character or FTS-syntax queries all work with no 500s. Reader UI passes every flow: suggestions, 'Search every word', Enter, results count, <mark> highlights, 'More results' (15 -> 30), clicking a result opens the article and hides the panel, 'back to reading', and Random/Home/monitor. No page errors. The frozen app builds and serves /_disckit/. bash -n passes, the workflow YAML is valid, and the icon is 1024x1024 RGBA with transparent corners. /api/kit/info and /api/kit/download are correct, and the KitSection renders both options with the icon loaded and v1.1.0. MAIN BUG: bm25 ranking always returns 0, so 'best matches first' only works when the search words appear in a title. Every body-only match comes back in insertion (alphabetical) order.

critical.issue: The FTS5 table is created with content='' plus detail=column. With that pair, bm25() returns 0.0 for every row. I confirmed this on the knots index ('paracord', 5/611 docs, all 0.0) and in a 5-row in-memory test on SQLite 3.40.1. content='' alone or detail=column alone scores correctly (-0.544 vs -0.264). So ORDER BY f.r does nothing, and results for body-only matches come back in rowid order. Example: q=sailor rope returns Adjustable bend, Adjustable grip hitch, Albright special... On real Wikipedia, any query with no title match will be alphabetical, not 'best matches first'.

minor.issue: int() raises ValueError in Handler._api, so the connection is dropped with no response. Wrap the parse in try/except and default to 0.

Terms with diacritics (q=lé) match through FTS remove_diacritics, but the snippet regex is diacritic-sensitive, so nothing is highlighted. Also, articles whose whole text equals the title (e.g. 'Braid length', a stub/redirect-like page) get an empty snippet, which shows as a blank

.

Prints the search index size in GB with 2 decimals, so small sources show '~0.00 GB' both with and without --no-fulltext. The plan() dict is correct (997225 bytes vs 0). The estimate is also about 45% low: 1.0 MB estimated vs about 1.8 MB actual index.db growth.

Each request sorts every matching row (ORDER BY lower(title)=?, title-subquery IN, bm25) before LIMIT. For common words on full Wikipedia (millions of matches) read from an M-DISC, this may take many seconds. Consider capping the candidate set or using FTS5's ORDER BY rank.

issues: Uses 'contain' even when the count is 1 ('1 article contain …'). Should be 'contains'.

action_items: Fix FTS ranking: change FTS_SCHEMA so bm25 works. Either drop content='' (keep detail=column; costs storage for a body copy) or keep content='' with detail=full (larger index but supports TF/phrases). Then re-check that 'Bowline' and body-only queries rank by relevance. Existing built discs would need a rebuild.
Guard the page param parse in reader/server.py _api (non-integer page currently kills the connection).
Optional: make snippet highlighting diacritic-insensitive (normalize with unicodedata NFKD for the regex), skip or fill empty snippets, and print the plan index size in MB when under 1 GB.

Rebuild /tmp/pyi frozen app after the fixes. The current binary (04:17:16) is older than volume.py (04:17:41) and lacks the title-boost ranking: its bowline query returns '62 knot' first and Bowline is not on page 1.
critical_code_review_comments: volume.py Volume.fulltext: the title-match ORDER BY term runs a second MATCH subquery per request. Fine for this ZIM, but on a 6M-doc index the IN-subquery plus full sort could be slow.

server.py Library.fulltext: 'more' is computed as len(results)==per_page summed across all text volumes. With more than one text volume this is wrong (2 volumes x 15 rows each). OK for the current 2-disc layout with one Text Disc.

shell.html: snippets and titles go through esc() before innerHTML, so injected article HTML is neutralized. esc() does not escape single quotes, but every attribute uses double quotes, so this is safe.

success_rate.backend: 96% (24/25 pytest; plus ranking bug found by manual analysis)

seed_data_creation: Temp builds in /tmp/ft (T, M, T2, M2) and /tmp/fz; pytest creates its own tempdirs
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_disckit_fulltext.py. It builds knots.zim twice and starts readers on free ports, about 4s total. To check ranking, run on index.db: SELECT d.title, bm25(fts,8.0,1.0) FROM fts JOIN docs d ON d.id=fts.rowid WHERE fts MATCH '"paracord"*'. All values should not be 0. For body-only ranking use q=sailor rope or q=climbing. Reader UI testids: reader-search, reader-search-all, reader-results, reader-results-count, reader-result, reader-results-more, #ftclose.
rca of the issue: SQLite FTS5 with a contentless table (content='') and detail=column cannot supply per-row phrase instance data to the bm25 auxiliary function, so bm25 returns 0.0 for every row. Repro: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE a USING fts5(body, content='', detail=column); insert 5 rows; SELECT bm25(a) ... MATCH 'apple' -> 0.0, 0.0. Mitigation: use detail=full with content='', or keep stored content with detail=column.
